note: Live-session recording of the screen scenes (series/tools/rec). Five portal screens (Power Automate and GitHub, two browser profiles). The GitHub repository is a private throwaway; the fine-grained token is pasted into the connection dialog by the owner and never written anywhere.
prepare: # owner signs in: the pac sign-in below and the browser profiles for labadmin (make.powerautomate.com, SharePoint) and the lab GitHub account. Nothing is typed or stored here.
pac auth create --name dev --environment $env:DEV_URL   # owner signs in, off camera

# owner (tenant, demo.md Setup 2-3): list IT Requests with SourceLink column and the category value Other; Power Automate Premium self-service trial for labadmin (custom connector needs a premium or trial licence); solution GitHubIntake (publisher contoso, prefix cts); GitHub repo it-automation-demo (private) with labels urgent and hardware; fine-grained token, 7 days, this repository only, Webhooks and Issues read/write

Push-Location .\src\connector; pac connector create --api-definition-file apiDefinition.swagger.json --api-properties-file apiProperties.json --solution-unique-name GitHubIntake; pac connector list; Pop-Location

# owner (demo.md Setup 4-5, 8): create the connection (GitHub user name + token), build the flow 'GitHub issue to IT request' in the solution and turn it on; then open the issue 'Laptop won't boot before a client demo' with the labels hardware and urgent and wait for the run

screens.name: connector
steps: Select environment DEV, open Solutions > GitHubIntake
Open the custom connector 'Contoso IT GitHub' and select Edit
On the Definition page show the trigger 'When an issue is opened' and the action 'Add a comment to an issue'
Scroll to the Policies section and show the three 'Set HTTP header' policies
Second capture, same scene: open the Security page: Basic authentication with the labels 'GitHub user name' and 'Fine-grained personal access token'
mask: environment URL and ID in the address bar
account name and tenant name in the top bar

screens.name: webhook
screens.account: the lab GitHub account (owner signs in)
steps: Turn the flow on in Power Automate first, then open the repository it-automation-demo > Settings > Webhooks
Show one webhook with event 'Issues' and content type application/json
Open Recent Deliveries and show a single delivery of event ping with response 200
mask: GitHub account name (repository owner, avatar, header)
webhook callback URL (it carries a signature)

screens.name: run
steps: Open the run history of 'GitHub issue to IT request' and the run started by the issue 'Laptop won't boot before a client demo' (labels hardware and urgent)
Expand the trigger output: action 'opened' and the issue title
Show 'Comment on issue' green and expand its output with the new comment URL
mask: environment URL and ID in the address bar
GitHub account name in the trigger output and the comment URL

screens.name: result
steps: Split view, left: the IT Requests list with the new item '[GitHub] Laptop won't boot before a client demo', Priority High, Status New, Source link set
Right: the GitHub issue with the comment from the token's account: 'Thanks, ... Contoso IT is tracking this as IT request #...' with the link
mask: tenant name in the SharePoint URL and header

screens.name: off
steps: Open the flow 'GitHub issue to IT request' and select Turn off; show the status Off
Open GitHub > it-automation-demo > Settings > Webhooks, refresh the page and show the list empty
If the webhook is still there, keep it on screen: the narration and README are fixed to match
mask: environment URL and ID in the address bar
webhook callback URL if it is still listed

teardown: # owner (GitHub): check that the webhook is gone; revoke the fine-grained token; delete the throwaway repository it-automation-demo

# owner (tenant): delete the connection and any copy of the flow; delete the junk and demo items from IT Requests; keep the solution GitHubIntake and the connector for episode 9, or delete both; end or keep the self-service Power Automate Premium trial (no cost)
